Gentle pressure, without pain. Insomnia lasting more than 3 weeks, snoring with breathing pauses or a depressed mood call for medical advice.

Very light pressure, mainly on the sternum. If you have osteoporosis, a pacemaker, anticoagulants or chest pain, do not do this. Pain, tightness or pressure in the chest (especially on exertion or radiating to the arm/jaw), shortness of breath, sweating or palpitations: emergency (112), not acupressure. Do not do this after chest surgery, with fractured ribs or after chest radiotherapy.
Moderate pressure, without sharp pain. In case of acute inflammation of the elbow or loss of strength, seek medical advice.

Pressure on the sides and front of the neck (arteries, thyroid), the eyes, enlarged lymph nodes, the back of the knee (popliteal fossa) and on bone; the abdomen during pregnancy; stop if tingling, numbness or sharp pain occurs.

Light pressure on the temple. With epilepsy or a history of seizures, do not apply repeated rhythmic presses on the head. If you have a new and severe headache, skip it. The stimulating effect may disturb sleep if done in the evening.
Pressure goes only on the bone, never on the eye. If you have glaucoma, recent eye surgery, a fragile retina or eye pain, skip it completely.

Pressure stays light over the veins; do not press behind the knee. During pregnancy, do not knead or press the calves (increased risk of thrombosis) and ask your doctor for approval; the sequence does not contain points marked "Avoid in pregnancy".

Cup the back of the neck with your fingers interlaced beneath it, and place your thumbs on both GB20, in the hollows below the occiput. With your thumbs or the tips of your middle fingers, also press BL10 at the same time, 1.3 cun lateral to the midline, just below the base of the skull, on the muscle next to the spine. Push with medium pressure (4–5/10) upward and toward the eyes, with long exhalations.

Grasp the lobe between thumb and index finger and gently massage it in small circles. Continue along the edge of the ear, upward, with slow movements. Then you may gently pull the ear sideways and downward a few times, without pain.

Grasp the muscle between your thumb and the rest of your fingers, lift it slightly and squeeze it gently, then let go, as if kneading soft dough. Move your hands slowly, with a rhythmic motion. If sharp pain occurs, reduce the pressure immediately.

Grasp a fold of skin between your thumbs and the other fingers and "roll" it forward, like a wave, moving your thumbs forward. If the skin does not lift easily or it hurts a lot, give up on that area. The movement is slow and without pinching.

Gently hold the hand, forearm or calf and shake quickly with a small amplitude, as if shaking a rope. The muscles stay relaxed, with no jerking and no strong pulling on the joint. Finish with a few slow strokes.

Place your index finger on ST36 and your middle finger on GB34, in the hollow in front of and below the head of the fibula, with the same hand, on the side of that leg. Press both at once with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10) for 60 seconds, then switch legs.

Place a small ball under each sole, at the junction of the front and middle thirds, in the depression between the two pads, where KI1 is located. Let the weight of your feet press down and make small slow rotations for 60 seconds.

Place one palm on the lower abdomen, over CV6, 1.5 cun below the navel, and the other palm on the lumbar area, on BL23, at waist level, lateral to the spine. Keep a warm contact, with very light pressure, for 90–120 seconds, breathing slowly.

Place the tip of the middle finger of one hand on Yintang, between the eyebrows, and that of the other hand on GV20, on the midline of the crown of the head. Press gently, lightly toward the bone, for 60 seconds, while breathing slowly (4 seconds on the inhale, 6 on the exhale).

Keep the ball on muscle only; if sharp pain occurs, lift your weight off the ball. During pregnancy, do not do this sequence (the lumbosacral area and buttocks are to be avoided: BL25, BL26, BL32, GB30), except with your doctor's approval.
